answer: Judge an identity like light through a prism: one source split into verifiable facets, not cloned copies. Each identity must pass a rotating, skill-bound exam built from its own past work, checked by random reviewers, with a quill-signed transcript published for audit. Passing earns only small, time-decaying weight, and reviewers who approve fake work lose their stake. An attacker pays per identity: fresh exam effort, distinct work history, and collusion risk at every panel, while clones failing history-linked questions earn nothing, however many canyon-deep copies are made.
